stem: A learner assumes a photoperiod cultivar and a day-neutral cultivar use the same dark-period trigger for flowering. Which correction is most accurate?
choices: Both are expected to use a similar critical dark-period signal because reproductive timing is primarily controlled by total daily darkness.
Photoperiod-sensitive and day-neutral flowering responses differ, so the same trigger assumption should not be applied to both.
Root-zone EC is the more reliable flowering trigger in both types because mineral demand changes precede visible reproductive development.
Photoperiod mainly affects vegetative structure, while reproductive timing is largely independent of recurring light-dark duration.
rationale: Photoperiod-sensitive and day-neutral genotypes differ in how reproductive development relates to photoperiod, so management assumptions should distinguish them.
